ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, it is known that $AB \parallel CD$, $\angle BAE = 30^\circ$, $\angle DCE = 60^\circ$, and $EF$, $EG$ trisect $\angle AEC$ (that is, $\angle AEF = \angle FEG = \angle GEC$). What is the measure of $\angle AEF$ in degrees?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Construct $EF' \parallel AB$ through point $E$, then $\angle BAE=\angle F'EA=30^\circ$,\\
because $AB\parallel CD$,\\
therefore $EF' \parallel CD$,\\
thus $\angle DCE=\angle F'EC=60^\circ$\\
Also, because $\angle AEC=\angle F'EA+\angle F'EC$,\\
thus $\angle AEC=90^\circ$,\\
because $EF, EG$ trisect $\angle AEC$ (i.e., $\angle AEF=\angle FEG=\angle GEC$)\\
therefore $\angle AEF=\boxed{30^\circ}$.

Since $EF$ and $EG$ trisect $\angle AEC$, it follows that $\angle AEF = \angle FEG = \angle GEC$, hence $\angle AEF = \boxed{30^\circ}$.
